B) RECIPE / THEME CONVENTION

3. Find every `*.css.ts` file under `overrides/app/`. For 2-3, dump them fully. Report: `defineRecipe` vs `defineSlotRecipe`, the `className` field, `base`/`variants`/`defaultVariants`, how `var(--zimm-*)` tokens are used, whether raw px values appear and whether they carry `audit-allow` comments.
4. How does a component consume its recipe at runtime? (e.g. `useRecipe`, `useSlotRecipe`, `chakra()`, `defineStyle`?) Give the exact import + call pattern with file:line.

C) NEAREST PRECEDENT — the PDP static product info work and the footer
5. `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` — full tree. Dump `index.tsx` and every file in `partials/`. Report how the PDP composes partials, what `renderHeader`/header slots exist, what `StaticProductHeader` does.
6. Find the footer component (`footerNavColumn` was mentioned in a PR body). Full tree + dump the component, its `.css.ts`, its story and test. This is cited as the pattern the swatch component followed.

D) TEST + STORY CONVENTIONS
7. Dump one representative `*.test.tsx` and one `*.stories.tsx` in full. Report: test runner (vitest?), render helper used (custom `renderWithProviders`? from where?), story format (CSF3? `Meta`/`StoryObj`?), what decorators/args are conventional.

E) TOKENS
8. Where are `--zimm-*` tokens defined? Find the token source files. Is there an `audit:tokens` script — what does it check (read `scripts/` for it)?

Return a dense report with absolute file:line citations. Include short code snippets ONLY where the exact text is load-bearing (recipe shape, import pattern, registration line). Distinguish VERIFIED from inferred.

1 # Components, Hooks & Storybook 2 3 Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this 4 project. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting 5 rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic 6 numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS 7 conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). 8 9 --- 10 11 ## Components 12 13 - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). 14 No default exports of anonymous functions. 15 - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, 16 `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. 17 - **Props type placement:** 18 - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. 19 - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling 20 files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with 21 other shared types worth co-locating. 22 - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. 23 - **JSDoc** is required on: 24 25 - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in 26 [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). 27 - Any exported hook. 28 - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. 29 30 Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. 31 32 - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). 33 - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions 34 for "I forgot to mark it optional." 35 - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get 36 these right at authoring time:** 37 - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). 38 - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs 39 an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to 40 announce. 41 - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, 42 `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` 43 attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an 44 `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which 45 is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). 46 47 --- 48 49 ## Composition — writing a "clean" component 50 51 Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline 52 state belongs in a custom hook instead. 53 54 - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and 55 avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent 56 paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** 57 — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so 58 treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not 59 something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding 60 those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new 61 dependency needed). 62 - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` 63 receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like 64 `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` 65 / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container 66 component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing 67 "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just 68 commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own 69 data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, 70 mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). 71 72 **Exception — Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks** (`useIntl`, `useUiCopy`) may 73 be called from any component, including presentational leaves. Both read from a Provider 74 mounted above the route tree, not from a per-page/per-component fetch — so calling one from 75 a leaf doesn't create the SSR/Storybook/parent-composition problem the rule above exists to 76 prevent, and doesn't multiply fetches the way an SDK hook would. `useUiCopy` 77 (`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`, Provider at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`) 78 is the reference example — `BottomBar` and `ZimmSubscribeSection` both call it directly 79 for microcopy while still receiving their actual business data as props. This exception is 80 narrow: it covers content that is identical for every consumer regardless of route/context, 81 not anything that varies per page. 82 83 **Their no-Provider behaviour differs, and it matters for tests and stories.** `useUiCopy` 84 degrades to fallback text — `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` — so a leaf calling 85 it renders with zero setup. `useIntl` **throws** (`react-intl`'s `invariantIntlContext`: 86 _"Could not find required `intl` object"_), and its `IntlProvider` is mounted by the **base 87 SFCC `_app`**, not by `_app-config` — a strictly narrower subtree. `.storybook/preview.tsx` 88 supplies one for stories precisely because of this; any Vitest test rendering a `useIntl` 89 consumer must wrap it too. An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed both hooks degrade 90 gracefully and that both Providers sit in `_app-config`; neither is true of `useIntl`. 91 - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook 92 (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: 93 94 - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal 95 the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). 96 - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial 97 meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a 98 one-line side effect. 99 100 This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as 101 a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable 102 coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?" 103 104 --- 105 106 ## Hooks 107 108 - **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file). 109 - **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`. 110 - **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type. 111 See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends. 112 - **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description. 113 114 --- 115 116 ## Storybook 117 118 Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable — 119 a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. 120 121 ### When a story is required 122 123 - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` 124 or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). 125 - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent 126 (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their 127 variants via the parent's stories. 128 - Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per 129 sub-section. 130 131 ### Categorisation 132 133 Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category: 134 135 | Category | What goes here | 136 | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 137 | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows | 138 | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. | 139 | `Layout/` | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo | 140 | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | 141 | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup | 142 | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account | 143 | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | 144 145 Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`). 146 147 Examples: 148 149 ```ts 150 export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ 151 export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅ 152 export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅ 153 export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅ 154 export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/ 155 export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/ 156 ``` 157 158 When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`, 159 CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`. 160 161 ### Story content 162 163 - Every story file has a `Default` named export. 164 - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not 165 for every possible prop combination. 166 - `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the 167 story is purely visual. 168

1	# Styling an Override Component
2	
3	How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
4	Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
5	different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
6	about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
7	rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
8	companion.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The hierarchy — reach for these in order
13	
14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
15	   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
16	2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
17	   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
18	   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
19	   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
20	   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
21	   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
22	   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
23	   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
24	   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
25	   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
26	   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
27	   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
28	3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
29	   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
30	   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
31	   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
32	   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
33	   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
34	   type" below.
35	4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
36	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
37	   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.
38	
39	**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
40	instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
41	constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
42	sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
43	before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
44	`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
45	(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
46	from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
47	contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
48	the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
49	existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
50	2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
51	full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
52	genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
53	Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
54	mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
55	Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
56	which is what `audit:tokens` is for.
57	
58	## Units
59	
60	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
61	  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
62	  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
63	  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
64	  comment for traceability.
65	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
66	  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
67	  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
68	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
69	  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
70	  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.
71	
72	## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy
73	
74	`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
75	plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
76	...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
77	value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
78	if only one of them is ever typed.
79	
80	`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
81	classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
82	`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
83	from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
84	numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
85	`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
86	derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
87	regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.
88	
89	## One canonical styling surface per component type
90	
91	Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
92	either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
93	beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
94	`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
95	`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
96	`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
97	structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
98	with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
99	button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
100	for any button, not a class.
101	
102	`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
103	massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
104	there's no interactive state to lose.
105	
106	## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component
107	
108	If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
109	override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
110	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
111	(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
112	base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
113	that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
114	import, which is correct for that file).
115	
116	The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
117	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
118	`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
119	server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
120	`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
121	resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
122	correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
123	version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
124	override and isn't.
125	
126	**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
127	import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
128	the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
129	calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
130	worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.
131	
132	An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
133	overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
134	etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.
135	
136	## Component-local tokens
137	
138	When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
139	`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
140	— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
141	`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
142	form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
143	used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
144	`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
145	so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.
146	
147	See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
148	`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
149	traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
150	Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
151	recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
152	SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
153	numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)
154	
155	**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
156	co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:
157	
158	```ts
159	[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
160	```
161	
162	The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
163	recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
164	responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
165	`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.
166	
167	When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
168	have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
169	than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
170	`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
171	sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.
172	
173	## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)
174	
175	If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
176	"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
177	node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
178	faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,

1	# Testing Conventions
2	
3	Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.
4	
5	**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
6	covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
7	decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
8	renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
9	Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
10	**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
11	elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
12	right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
13	component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
14	component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
15	and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
16	`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
17	resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
18	render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
19	(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
20	below for single-parent internal components still applies there.
21	
22	| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
23	|---|---|---|---|---|
24	| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
25	| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
26	| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |
27	
28	> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.
29

31	
32	## What to test (and what to skip)
33	
34	Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:
35	
36	- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
37	- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
38	- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
39	- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
40	- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
41	- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
42	- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches
43

45	
46	## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)
47	
48	### File layout
49	
50	Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:
51	
52	```
53	overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
54	overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
55	overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
56	overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
57	```
58	
59	Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
60	(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).
61	
62	### Structure
63	
64	- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
65	- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
66	- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
67	- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.
68	
69	### Mocking
70	
71	- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
72	- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
73	- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
74	- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
75	- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
76	  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
77	  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
78	  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
79	  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
80	  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
81	  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,
82	  if an assertion depends on an accessible name the real `ZimmIcon` would carry (e.g. a
83	  fallback `<span aria-label>` with no wrapping interactive element), forward the relevant
84	  props instead of returning `null`. See `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and
85	  `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for both variants.
86	
87	### Commerce SDK hooks
88	
89	Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.
90	
91	### What NOT to write at this layer
92	
93	- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
94	- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
95	- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks

99	## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)
100	
101	### When to use `play`
102	
103	Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:
104	
105	- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
106	- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
107	- Focus moves correctly through a flow
108	- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output
109	
110	If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.
111	
112	### Pattern
113	
114	```tsx
115	import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'
116	
117	export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
118	    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
119	        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
120	        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
121	        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
122	        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
123	        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
124	    }
125	}
126	```
127	
128	- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
129	- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
130	- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.
131	
132	### What NOT to write at this layer
133	
134	- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
135	- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright

139	## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)
140	
141	### Workflow
142	
143	E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):
144	
145	1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
146	2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
147	3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved
148	
149	This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."
150	
151	### File layout
152	
153	```
154	e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
155	e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
156	e2e/support/
157	  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
158	  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
159	e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
160	```
161	
162	Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
163	(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
164	runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
165	tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
166	[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.
167	
168	### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)
169	
170	`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
171	files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:
172	
173	- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
174	  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
175	  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
176	  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
177	  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
178	  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
179	  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
180	- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
181	  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
182	  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
183	  area's allow-list**. A single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
184	  claimed yet) resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` instead — `e2e-localhost` does not run at all on
185	  that PR (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request; previously fell back to running the
186	  full suite on every such PR). `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact
187	  path lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
188	- **This is a deliberate coverage trade-off, not a gap to silently work around.** A
189	  `develop`-targeted PR that can't be scoped to one area gets no PR-time E2E run at all — only
190	  unit tests / Storybook, plus BrowserStack if the PR references a Jira key with a tagged spec.
191	  Full/non-P0 regression coverage for that PR is deferred to the existing post-merge P0 gates
192	  (`deploy-test.yml`'s Test-tier gate, `digital-sit.yml`'s `playwright-p0` on `release/**`) —
193	  which only cover P0-tagged journeys, a subset of the full suite. A non-P0 regression introduced
194	  by a shared/global-path change can therefore reach `develop` before anything catches it. This
195	  was accepted deliberately to stop the full suite running on every PR touching a shared path
196	  (the single largest line item in this repo's CI-minutes usage) — revisit if it causes real
197	  regressions to slip through in practice.
198	- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff, unchanged — a release
199	  PR aggregates a whole sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
200	  [releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md). This skip-instead-of-full
201	  behavior only applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
202	- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
203	  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
204	  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage silently — it just means that
205	  spec's PRs get `e2e_scope: skip` (no PR-time run) instead of the scoping optimisation, same as
206	  any other unclaimed path.
207	
208	### BrowserStack story scoping
209	
210	`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
211	what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
212	target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
213	below for why):
214	
215	- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
216	  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
217	  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
218	- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
219	  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
220	  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).
221	
222	Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
223	`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.
224	
225	**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
226	integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
227	Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
228	flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
229	results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
230	(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
231	the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
232	per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
233	result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
234	Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
235	story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
236	confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
237	attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
238	evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
239	execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.
240	
241	**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
242	GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
243	**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
244	GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
245	what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
246	PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
247	itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
248	`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
249	`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
250	`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
251	`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
252	triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
253	`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
254	directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
255	the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
256	has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
257	carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
258	`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
259	(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.
260	
261	**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
262	derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
263	scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
264	`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
265	grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
266	the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
267	`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
268	Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
269	that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
270	recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
271	workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
272	`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
273	Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
274	this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
275	independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
276	guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
277	documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
278	`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
279	job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
280	fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
281	correctly, 2026-08-25).
282	
283	**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
284	Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
285	Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
286	mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
287	to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
288	result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
289	real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed
290	`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
291	does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.
292	
293	The only real fix is to stop the "wrong" project from ever collecting that test at all, which
294	`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
295	project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
296	platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
297	genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
298	`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
299	`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
300	per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
301	ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
302	different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
303	exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
304	regardless of what its title says.
305	
306	**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
307	`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
308	header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
309	production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
310	the one real case this repo has needed so far.
311	
312	**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
313	`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
314	currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
315	`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
316	artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
317	see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code.
318	
319	**No fallback to the static test tier when that artifact is missing (removed 2026-08-26,
320	CodeRabbit flagged this correctly)** — an earlier version of this job silently fell back to the
321	static `test`-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` whenever `deploy-preview.yml` failed or hadn't finished. That
322	let a develop PR whose own deployment genuinely failed still produce a green, story-tagged Zephyr
323	execution (and a possible auto-filed Jira defect) that proved nothing about the PR's own code —
324	the exact condition the fallback existed to tolerate was the one that made its result meaningless.
325	`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s "Resolve BrowserStack test target" step now fails the job loudly
326	(`::error::` + `exit 1`) instead when the hostname artifact is missing, whether that's because
327	Deploy Preview failed outright or succeeded but didn't reach the artifact-upload step. Same
328	principle [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)'s Graceful Degradation section already states for
329	checkout/payment: never silently substitute a different flow, surface an explicit error instead.
330	A cancelled Deploy Preview run is the one case with nothing to fail loudly about — the job-level
331	`if:` skips the whole job entirely rather than running it just to hit this failure, since there's
332	no meaningful error to surface for a run nobody asked to complete.
333	
334	**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
335	that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
336	Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
337	other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
338	up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
339	even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
340	inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
341	itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
342	separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
343	the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
344	polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
345	`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
346	job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
347	for.
348	
349	- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
350	  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
351	  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
352	- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
353	  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
354	  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
355	  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
356	  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
357	  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
358	  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
359	  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
360	  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
361	  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
362	  run — **but this is a fail-open check, not an unconditional guarantee** (CodeRabbit flagged the
363	  distinction correctly, 2026-08-26): the normal path is that a Jira-tagged PR touching nothing
364	  e2e-relevant genuinely skips BrowserStack. If the QA-run lookup or the `e2e-scope` artifact
365	  download itself fails for any reason (the run isn't found yet, the artifact expired, an API
366	  hiccup), this step assumes relevant rather than adding a retry loop to chase the optimisation —
367	  so in that specific failure case, a Jira-tagged PR can still run BrowserStack even when its
368	  changes weren't e2e-relevant. Worst case is one avoidable BrowserStack run, not a correctness
369	  problem, but it's a real exception to the "doesn't pay for a BrowserStack run" claim, not a
370	  universal guarantee.
371	- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
372	  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
373	  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
374	- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
375	  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
376	  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
377	  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
378	  by `e2e-localhost`.
379	- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
380	  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
381	  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
382	  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
383	  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
384	  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
385	  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
386	  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.
387	
388	### Multi-region fixtures
389	
390	Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.
391	
392	```ts
393	test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
394	    for (const site of SITES) {
395	        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
396	    }
397	})
398	```
399	
400	### Page Object Model
401	
402	Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:
403	
404	1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
405	2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
406	3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).
407	
408	Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.
409	
410	### What NOT to write at this layer
411	
412	- Pure logic — that's Vitest
413	- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
414	- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.
415	
416	---
417	
418	## Test config files are Tier 1
419	
420	`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js` are
421	**frozen** ([frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)). Do not modify them in a feature PR — config drift breaks every contributor's harness. Changes go through the Integration team.
422	
423	---
424	
425	## Quick checklist before opening a PR
426	
427	- [ ] New component → has `*.stories.tsx`
428	- [ ] Non-obvious logic → has `*.test.ts`
429	- [ ] New user journey → has a `.feature` file (Playwright spec follows after Lead QA sign-off)
430	- [ ] `npm run test` passes locally
431	- [ ] No new MSW handlers in production-path code
432	- [ ] No edits to Tier 1 test config files
